evals.prompt: coordinate a few agents to migrate every call site of this API and keep me in the loop at each phase
evals.expected_output: Orchestration driven from the main context: work decomposed into tasks, sub-agents dispatched per unit of work, and a phase gate reported to the user before the next phase starts, with each phase committed through gh-commit only after the user's go-ahead
expectations: Keeps all top-level dispatching in the main context rather than delegating orchestration to a nested agent

Records the units of work as tasks (the planner's tasks inside the planner→worker loop, or its own TaskCreate items for delegated work outside it) and checks TaskList before deciding what to delegate next
Inside the planner→worker loop, does not pre-mark worker tasks in_progress or add its own items to the planner's task list
Dispatches one worker per pending task instead of handing a worker several tasks at once
Stops at each phase boundary that has manual checks and reports in the Phase [N] Complete — Ready for Manual Verification shape, then waits for the user to confirm the manual steps
Never checks off a manual verification item on the user's behalf
Commits each confirmed phase from the main context via Skill('gh-commit'), relying on gh-commit's own confirmation; workers do not commit

evals.prompt: run this refactor end to end, fan the investigation out and report back
evals.expected_output: A long-horizon loop where investigation is fanned out to parallel sub-agents and only condensed results return to the main context
expectations: Launches the independent investigation agents in a single message so they run concurrently
Writes self-contained prompts — each sub-agent sees only what the prompt carries, not this conversation
Continues an already-running agent with SendMessage rather than re-spawning it
Delegates verbose commands rather than running them inline, or wraps them via the Bash tool with backpressure.sh passing the wrapped command as separate arguments
Does not attempt the work itself while waiting on a sub-agent
Does not pass a run_in_background parameter to the Agent tool

evals.prompt: spawn parallel sub-agents to document how auth works in this repo
evals.expected_output: Not an orchestration task: documenting current behavior is one CRISPY research phase, and the phase skills are manual-only, so Claude points the user to /research-codebase (or /ask-questions to start a task directory) instead of opening an orchestration loop
expectations: Recognizes this as one CRISPY research phase, not a multi-phase long-horizon task, despite the parallel sub-agent phrasing
Names the /research-codebase command (or /ask-questions to start the task) for the user to run, since the phase skills are manual-only and Claude does not invoke them itself
Creates no task list and no phase gates for what is a single-phase request

evals.prompt: /orchestrate .agents/artifacts/feat-ENG-123-csv-export flow: design — the directory has 01-request-csv-export.html, 02-research-questions-csv-export.html, 03-research-csv-export.html, 04-design-discussion-csv-export.html, and 05-structure-outline-csv-export.html with three slices, each carrying Automated and Manual verification. There is no spec.
evals.expected_output: The implement step runs from the task directory: the planner is dispatched with the task directory, decomposes the outline's three slices (the outline outranks the design discussion), the worker loop stops at a gate after each slice using that slice's verification lists, and each confirmed slice is committed and marked ✅ in the outline
expectations: Dispatches the planner with the task directory path rather than pasting document contents or picking a document itself
The planner treats the structure outline as the governing document (spec > structure outline > TDD > PRD > design discussion > research > request) and creates one phase per slice
Dispatches one worker per pending task and runs tasks from the next slice only after the current slice's gate is confirmed
Reports each gate in exactly the Phase [N] Complete — Ready for Manual Verification shape, listing the slice's automated commands with results and its manual steps, then waits
Never checks off a manual verification item on the user's behalf
After the user confirms a slice, commits its changes via Skill('gh-commit') with gh-commit's own confirmation, leaving .agents/artifacts/ unstaged

Updates 05-structure-outline-csv-export.html in place through Skill('output-html'): checks the passed automated items and the user-confirmed manual items, and marks the slice's Implementation Overview item and heading ✅
When all three slices are done, reports what changed, the checks run, and any manual verification still pending, and offers to open the updated outline for review

evals.prompt: /orchestrate .agents/artifacts/fix-retry-backoff flow: tdd — the directory has a request, research, and an approved 04-tdd-retry-backoff.md; no structure outline or spec.
evals.expected_output: With no outline or spec, the planner decomposes the TDD's scope as a single phase and there is one gate at the end listing the TDD's verification expectations
expectations: Dispatches the planner with the task directory; the TDD governs because no spec or outline exists
Runs the worker loop without intermediate phase gates, since the design scope is a single phase
Stops once at the end and reports in the Phase [N] Complete — Ready for Manual Verification shape, with the manual steps drawn from the TDD's verification expectations
Does not invent outline slices or a spec to create extra gates
Commits through Skill('gh-commit') only after the user confirms the final gate

evals.prompt: /orchestrate .agents/artifacts/feat-ENG-140-audit-export flow: tdd — 05-structure-outline-audit-export.md has two slices. Slice 1's Manual verification reads "None — fully covered by automated checks"; Slice 2 lists two manual UI checks.
evals.expected_output: Slice 1 continues without a pause once its automated checks pass (after recording progress and offering the commit); the loop pauses at Slice 2 for manual verification
expectations: After Slice 1's tasks complete, confirms its automated verification passed before treating the phase as done
Does not stop for manual verification after Slice 1, since it has no manual checks; checks Slice 1's automated items and marks it ✅ in the outline via Skill('output-markdown')
Commits Slice 1 via Skill('gh-commit') once its automated checks pass, through gh-commit's own confirmation
Pauses after Slice 2 with the Phase [N] Complete — Ready for Manual Verification report listing its two manual checks, then waits

evals.prompt: /orchestrate .agents/artifacts/feat-ENG-123-csv-export flow: design — new session. The outline shows Slice 1 ✅ with all items checked; Slices 2 and 3 are unchecked and both have manual checks. Run the remaining slices straight through, I'll test everything at the end.
evals.expected_output: Implementation resumes from Slice 2 (the first incomplete slice) and runs Slices 2 and 3 continuously, verifying automated checks between them and leaving the manual checks pending for the final report
expectations: Resumes from Slice 2, the first incomplete slice; does not re-implement Slice 1, which is marked ✅
Verifies each slice's automated checks before moving to the next slice, turning any failure into a bug-fix task
Does not pause for manual verification between Slices 2 and 3, because the user asked for a continuous run
Leaves the unconfirmed manual checks unchecked in the outline and does not mark Slices 2 and 3 ✅ until the user confirms them
The final report lists what changed, the checks run with results, and the manual verification still pending for both slices

evals.prompt: /orchestrate .agents/artifacts/feat-ENG-123-csv-export — the export from slice 2 drops the last row when the file has no trailing newline. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The iterate-implementation path: reproduce the bug, fix it through a worker task with a regression test, update affected outline sections and validation markers, and commit through the gate rule
expectations: Reads the task directory's documents and the current diff, then reproduces the reported behavior before changing anything
Creates a worker task for the fix that includes a regression test, dispatching the debugger first when the cause is not obvious
Keeps the outline's validation markers accurate (unchecks an item the bug invalidates) and updates affected outline sections in place if the agreed result changes
Asks at most one targeted question, with a recommended answer, only if the expected behavior is unclear
Commits the fix via Skill('gh-commit') only with the user's go-ahead

Names `/create-tdd .agents/artifacts/feat-ENG-123-csv-export flow: prd-tdd` as the next command
